1726.summary: The class explores the life of Abraham, focusing on his faith and obedience, particularly his departure from Ur and Haran to Canaan. It emphasizes the importance of separating from worldly influences and trusting God's unseen promises.

1727.summary: The class discusses Abraham's decision to separate from Lot and his subsequent test of faith in offering Isaac as a sacrifice, emphasizing the importance of obedience and faith in God's commands.

1728.summary: The class examines patterns in the lives of biblical figures like Moses and Samson, showing how even the most faithful servants can fall into disobedience and temptation. True faithfulness lies not in avoiding failure but in repenting, persisting in prayer, and continuing to serve God after discipline.

1729.summary: The class explores the background of John the Baptist, focusing on his parents, Zacharias and Elizabeth, and their roles in the temple. It emphasizes the importance of faith and prayer, even when desires are not immediately fulfilled, and draws parallels to the responsibilities and duties of the Aaronic priesthood.
